q-106277.name: Question 1
q-106277.problem:
$$
⟨\text{_______}\,,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩
$$

The fundamental vector product of the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis for $x\in [0,\pi ]$ is given above. What is the $1$st component of the product?
q-106277.worked_solution:
Notice that $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\ge 0$ for all $x\in [0,\pi ].$ The parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨x,f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,(x,\theta )\in D\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ and

$$
D={(x,\theta )\,:\,0\le x\le \pi ,\,0\le \theta <2\pi }.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂x},\,\frac{∂y}{∂x},\,\frac{∂z}{∂x}⟩=⟨1,\,{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\ {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂y}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂z}{∂\theta }⟩=⟨0,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨f{f}^{′}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +f{f}^{′}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨f{f}^{′},\,-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f=\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ we obtain ${f}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ So, finally, we conclude that the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{x}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

⟨_______,−sin⁡xcos⁡θ,−sin⁡xsin⁡θ⟩

The fundamental vector product of the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve y=sin⁡x by 2π radians about the x-axis for x∈[0,π] is given above. What is the 1st component of the product?

a
sin⁡xcos⁡x
b
sin2⁡x
c
cos2⁡x
d
cos⁡x
e
sin⁡x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that y=sin⁡x≥0 for all x∈[0,π]. The parametrization of our surface of revolution is

r=⟨x,f(x)cos⁡θ,f(x)sin⁡θ⟩,(x,θ)∈D

where f(x)=sin⁡x, and

D={(x,θ):0≤x≤π,0≤θ<2π}.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

rx′=⟨∂x∂x,∂y∂x,∂z∂x⟩=⟨1,f′cos⁡θ,f′sin⁡θ⟩rθ′=⟨∂x∂θ,∂y∂θ,∂z∂θ⟩=⟨0,−fsin⁡θ,fcos⁡θ⟩

Next, the fundamental vector product is

rx′×rθ′=|ijk1f′cos⁡θf′sin⁡θ0−fsin⁡θfcos⁡θ|=⟨|f′cos⁡θf′sin⁡θ−fsin⁡θfcos⁡θ|,−|1f′sin⁡θ0fcos⁡θ|,|1f′cos⁡θ0−fsin⁡θ|⟩=⟨ff′cos2⁡θ+ff′sin2⁡θ,−fcos⁡θ,−fsin⁡θ⟩=⟨ff′,−fcos⁡θ,−fsin⁡θ⟩.

Since f=sin⁡x, we obtain f′=cos⁡x. So, finally, we conclude that the fundamental vector product is

rx′×rθ′=⟨sin⁡xcos⁡x,−sin⁡xcos⁡θ,−sin⁡xsin⁡θ⟩.

q-161037.problem:
$$
r(z,\theta )=⟨\sqrt{{z}^{2}-1}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\text{__________},\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $r(z,\theta )$ above parametrizes the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve $x=\sqrt{{z}^{2}-1}$ by  $2\pi $ radians about the $z$-axis for $z\in [1,5].$ What is the second  component of $r?$
q-161037.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14118233/assets/d3302b5f4ea4c0387d70ac8f78e03e486fff9579f1a6b5e5cec08a31cde76af3.png)

 

A point $(x,y,z)$ on the surface generated by rotating the graph of $x=f(z)$ by $2\pi $ radians about the $z$-axis has the position vector

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨f(z)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,f(z)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩,\,z\in [a,b],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that $x=f(z)=\sqrt{{z}^{2}-1}\ge 0$ for all $z\in [1,5].$   

So, the parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
r(z,\theta )=⟨\sqrt{{z}^{2}-1}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\sqrt{{z}^{2}-1}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩,\,z\in [1,5],\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Therefore, the second component of $r$ is $\sqrt{{z}^{2}-1}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .$

\begin{aligned}{r}_{z}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂z},\,\frac{∂y}{∂z},\,\frac{∂z}{∂z}⟩=⟨{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂y}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂z}{∂\theta }⟩=⟨f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{z}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-{f}^{′}f{sin}^{2}⁡\theta -{f}^{′}f{cos}^{2}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-{f}^{′}f⟩.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

⟨z−1sin⁡θ,z−1cos⁡θ,_______⟩

The fundamental vector product of the surface of revolution generated by rotating the curve y=z−1 by 2π radians about the z-axis for z∈[1,10] is given above. What is the 3rd component of the product?

a
−12
b
12z−1
c
−(z−1)2
d
z−12
e
−2(z−1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that y=z−1≥0 for all z∈[1,10]. The parametrization of our surface of revolution is

r=⟨f(z)sin⁡θ,f(z)cos⁡θ,z⟩,(z,θ)∈D

where f(z)=z−1, and

D={(z,θ):1≤z≤10,0≤θ<2π}.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

rz′=⟨∂x∂z,∂y∂z,∂z∂z⟩=⟨f′sin⁡θ,f′cos⁡θ,1⟩rθ′=⟨∂x∂θ,∂y∂θ,∂z∂θ⟩=⟨fcos⁡θ,−fsin⁡θ,0⟩

Next, the fundamental vector product is

rz′×rθ′=|ijkf′sin⁡θf′cos⁡θ1fcos⁡θ−fsin⁡θ0|=⟨|f′cos⁡θ1−fsin⁡θ0|,−|f′sin⁡θ1fcos⁡θ0|,|f′sin⁡θf′cos⁡θfcos⁡θ−fsin⁡θ|⟩=⟨fsin⁡θ,fcos⁡θ,−f′fsin2⁡θ−f′fcos2⁡θ⟩=⟨fsin⁡θ,fcos⁡θ,−f′f⟩.

Since f=z−1, we obtain f′=12z−1. So, finally, we conclude that the fundamental vector product is

rz′×rθ′=⟨z−1sin⁡θ,z−1cos⁡θ,−12⟩.

q-161090.name: Question 4
q-161090.problem: Use a fundamental vector product to determine which of the following integrals gives the surface area generated when the curve $x=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{y}{2})$ is rotated by $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis for $y\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$
q-161090.worked_solution:
Notice that $x=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{y}{2})\ge 0$ for all $y\in [-\pi ,\pi ].$ The parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨f(y)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y,\,f(y)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩,\,(y,\theta )\in D\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{y}{2}),$ and

$$
D={(y,\theta )\,:\,-\pi \le y\le \pi ,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi }.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{y}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂y},\,\frac{∂y}{∂y}\,\frac{∂z}{∂y}⟩=⟨{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,1,\,{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\ {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂y}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂z}{∂\theta }⟩=⟨-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,0,\,f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{y}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 0 & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ 0 & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f{f}^{′}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -f{f}^{′}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ,\,f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f{f}^{′},\,f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{y}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖ & =\sqrt{(f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(-f{f}^{′})^{2}+(f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{f}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+{f}^{2}({f}^{′})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{f}^{2}+{f}^{2}({f}^{′})^{2}} \\  & =f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{y}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖\text{d}y\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={∬}_{D}f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}\theta \,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\cdot \theta \,{|}_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(y)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{y}{2}),$ we obtain ${f}^{′}(y)=-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{y}{2}).$ So, finally, we conclude that our expression for the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi {\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\text{d}y & =2\pi {\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{y}{2})\sqrt{1+{(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{y}{2}))}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{y}{2})\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{4}{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{y}{2})}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161096.problem: Use a fundamental vector product to determine which of the following integrals gives the surface area generated when the curve $x={z}^{4}+1$ is rotated by $2\pi $ radians about the $z$-axis for $z\in [-1,1].$
q-161096.worked_solution:
Notice that $x={z}^{4}+1\ge 0$ for all $z\in [-1,1].$ The parametrization of our surface of revolution is

$$
\begin{aligned}r=⟨f(z)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,f(z)\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z⟩,\,(z,\theta )\in D\end{aligned}
$$

where $f(z)=1+{z}^{4},$ and

$$
D={(z,\theta )\,:\,-1\le z\le 1,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi }.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{z}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂z},\,\frac{∂y}{∂z},\,\frac{∂z}{∂z}⟩=⟨{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂y}{∂\theta },\,\frac{∂z}{∂\theta }⟩=⟨-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,f(y)\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{z}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ {f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & 1 \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & {f}^{′}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ -f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,{f}^{′}f{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{f}^{′}f{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ⟩ \\  & =⟨-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,{f}^{′}f⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

  

and

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{z}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖ & =\sqrt{(-f\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(-f\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}+({f}^{′}f)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{f}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )+{f}^{2}({f}^{′})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{f}^{2}+{f}^{2}({f}^{′})^{2}} \\  & =f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{z}^{′}\times {r}_{\theta }^{′}‖\text{d}z\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={∬}_{D}f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}\theta \,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\cdot \theta \,{|}_{0}^{2\pi }\,\text{d}z \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(z)=1+{z}^{4},$ we obtain ${f}^{′}(z)=4{z}^{3}.$ So, finally, we conclude that our expression for the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}f\sqrt{1+({f}^{′})^{2}}\,\text{d}z & =2\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}(1+{z}^{4})\sqrt{1+(4{z}^{3})^{2}}\,\text{d}z \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-1}^{1}(1+{z}^{4})\sqrt{1+16{z}^{6}}\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5

Use a fundamental vector product to determine which of the following integrals gives the surface area generated when the curve x=z4+1 is rotated by 2π radians about the z-axis for z∈[−1,1].

a
π∫−11(1+z4)1+8z6dz
b
2π∫−11(1+z4)1+8z6dz
c
π∫−11(1+z4)1+16z6dz
d
2π∫−11(1+z4)1+16z8dz
e
2π∫−11(1+z4)1+16z6dz
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that x=z4+1≥0 for all z∈[−1,1]. The parametrization of our surface of revolution is

r=⟨f(z)cos⁡θ,f(z)sin⁡θ,z⟩,(z,θ)∈D

where f(z)=1+z4, and

D={(z,θ):−1≤z≤1,0≤θ≤2π}.

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

rz′=⟨∂x∂z,∂y∂z,∂z∂z⟩=⟨f′cos⁡θ,f′sin⁡θ,1⟩rθ′=⟨∂x∂θ,∂y∂θ,∂z∂θ⟩=⟨−fsin⁡θ,f(y)cos⁡θ,0⟩

Next, the fundamental vector product is

rz′×rθ′=|ijkf′cos⁡θf′sin⁡θ1−fsin⁡θfcos⁡θ0|=⟨|f′sin⁡θ1fcos⁡θ0|,−|f′cos⁡θ1−fsin⁡θ0|,|f′cos⁡θf′sin⁡θ−fsin⁡θfcos⁡θ|⟩=⟨−fcos⁡θ,−fsin⁡θ,f′fcos2⁡θ+f′fsin2⁡θ⟩=⟨−fcos⁡θ,−fsin⁡θ,f′f⟩.

and

‖rz′×rθ′‖=(−fcos⁡θ)2+(−fsin⁡θ)2+(f′f)2=f2(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)+f2(f′)2=f2+f2(f′)2=f1+(f′)2.

Therefore, the surface area is

A=∬SdS=∬D‖rz′×rθ′‖dzdθ=∬Df1+(f′)2dzdθ=∫−11f1+(f′)2∫02πdθdz=∫−11f1+(f′)2⋅θ|02πdz=2π∫−11f1+(f′)2dz.

Since f(z)=1+z4, we obtain f′(z)=4z3. So, finally, we conclude that our expression for the surface area is

2π∫−11f1+(f′)2dz=2π∫−11(1+z4)1+(4z3)2dz=2π∫−11(1+z4)1+16z6dz.
